hints: Focus on what hot, concentrated, acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$ does to every $\text{C}=\text{C}$ bond, it cleaves it completely to carbonyls and then oxidises aldehydes further.
Notice the difference between $=\text{CH}-$ which ends up as a carboxylic acid, and $=\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)-$ which must end up as a ketone of the form $\text{CH}_3-\text{C}(=\text{O})-$.
Count how many alkene carbons carry a methyl group in $\beta$-carotene, and think carefully about whether the two ring openings give one or two ketone-containing fragments each.
walkthrough:
**Recall vigorous alkene cleavage**

Hot, concentrated, acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$ breaks every $\text{C}=\text{C}$ bond. Think of cleavage, not addition.

$$\text{R-CH}=\text{CH-R'} \rightarrow \text{R-COOH} + \text{HOOC-R'}$$
$$\text{R-C}(\text{CH}_3)=\text{CH-R'} \rightarrow \text{R-CO-CH}_3 + \text{HOOC-R'}$$

**Sort the two types of alkene carbon**

If the alkene carbon has one H, $=\text{CH}-$, it first forms $\text{-CHO}$ then is oxidised further to $\text{-COOH}$. It does not give a ketone.

If the alkene carbon has no H but has a methyl and another carbon, $=\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)-$, it forms $\text{CH}_3-\text{C}(=\text{O})-$, a ketone which resists further oxidation.

**Count the methyl-substituted alkene carbons**

Look at the structure. Ignore the saturated gem-dimethyl $\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)_2$ groups, they are not on $\text{C}=\text{C}$.

There are 4 methyl groups on the open chain $\text{C}=\text{C}$ bonds plus 1 methyl on each of the two ring $\text{C}=\text{C}$ bonds. That is 6 $=\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)-$ carbons in total.

**Convert carbons to ketone-containing molecules**

Each of the 4 chain $=\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)-$ units is cut out as a small fragment like $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-CH}= $ cut to $\text{CH}_3\text{-CO-COOH}$ type. That is 4 separate molecules, each containing a ketone.

Each cyclohexene ring is opened at its $\text{C}=\text{C}$ bond but stays joined through its three $\text{CH}_2$ groups. After the next chain $\text{C}=\text{C}$ is also cut, each ring gives one larger fragment containing ketone groups. That is 2 more molecules.

Total ketone-containing product molecules $= 4 + 2 = 6$.

options.A: 4 counts only the open-chain methyl-substituted double bonds. It forgets that the two ring $\text{C}=\text{C}$ bonds also each have a $\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)$ carbon that gives a ketone on ring opening.
options.B: Correct. The 4 chain $=\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)-$ carbons give 4 ketone-containing fragments, and the 2 ring $=\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)-$ carbons give 2 ring-opened ketone-containing fragments, total 6.
options.C: 9 is too high. It may come from counting double bonds or methyl groups incorrectly, for example counting saturated gem-dimethyl groups or $=\text{CH}-$ carbons which give acids, not ketones.
options.D: 11 is the approximate total number of $\text{C}=\text{C}$ bonds cleaved, not the number of ketone products. Most cleavage ends from $=\text{CH}-$ give carboxylic acids, not ketones.
